_about: Gospels and Acts, part A: each step tied to its place; road waypoints the text never mentions removed; lake crossings marked as boat trips; missing moments added.

set.note: Nazareth and Jerusalem are known; Luke says only that the family went a day's journey before missing him, so that spot is approximate.

steps.label: Up for the Passover
steps.copy: When Jesus is twelve, the family goes up to Jerusalem for the feast, as they do every year.

steps.label: Left behind
steps.copy: Heading home, they travel a day before realizing he isn't with them, and they turn back to look for him.

steps.label: Found in the temple
steps.copy: After three days they find him in the temple, sitting among the teachers, listening and asking questions.

steps.label: Home to Nazareth
steps.copy: He goes down to Nazareth with them and is obedient to them, growing in wisdom and stature.

steps.label: Setting out to persecute
steps.copy: Still breathing threats against the disciples, Saul gets letters to arrest believers in Damascus.

steps.label: The light from heaven
steps.copy: As he nears Damascus a light from heaven flashes around him, and a voice asks, “Saul, Saul, why do you persecute Me?”

steps.label: Led into the city
steps.copy: Blinded, he is led by the hand into Damascus, and for three days he neither eats nor drinks.

steps.label: Ananias
steps.copy: Ananias lays his hands on him; something like scales falls from his eyes, and he is baptized.

set.note: Luke places the meeting on the desert road that goes down from Jerusalem to Gaza; the exact spot is not recorded.

steps.label: Sent to the Gaza road
steps.copy: An angel sends Philip to the desert road, where an Ethiopian official sits in his chariot reading.

steps.label: The chariot and Isaiah
steps.copy: He is reading Isaiah, and Philip tells him the good news about Jesus, beginning with that very passage.

steps.label: Baptized by the road
steps.copy: They come to some water and the man is baptized; he goes on his way rejoicing.

steps.label: Found at Azotus
steps.copy: Philip appears at Azotus and preaches the gospel in all the towns until he reaches Caesarea.

steps.label: Leaving Judea
steps.copy: He leaves Judea for Galilee, and he has to pass through Samaria.

steps.label: The woman at the well
steps.copy: Tired at Jacob's well near Sychar, Jesus offers a Samaritan woman living water.

steps.label: Samaritans believe
steps.copy: He stays two days, and many more believe: “This man truly is the Christ, the Savior of the world.”

steps.label: On to Galilee
steps.copy: After two days he goes on to Galilee and comes again to Cana.

steps.label: To the region of Tyre
steps.copy: He goes away to the region of Tyre and wants no one to know, but he cannot stay hidden.

steps.label: The Syrophoenician woman
steps.copy: A Gentile woman begs him for her daughter; because of her answer, the demon leaves the girl.

steps.label: Through Sidon
steps.copy: He goes on through Sidon.

steps.label: Into the Decapolis
steps.copy: Back at the Sea of Galilee in the region of the Ten Cities, he heals a man who is deaf and can hardly speak.

steps.label: Across to the other side
steps.copy: When evening comes, Jesus says, “Let us cross to the other side,” and they set out in the boat.

steps.label: Peace, be still
steps.copy: A furious storm rises; he rebukes the wind and the sea, and it becomes perfectly calm.

steps.label: Among the tombs
steps.copy: On the far shore a man with an unclean spirit runs to meet him, and Jesus sets him free.

steps.label: Sent from Jerusalem
steps.copy: Hearing that Samaria has received the word of God, the apostles send Peter and John.

steps.label: Prayer for the Spirit
steps.copy: They pray and lay hands on the believers, who receive the Holy Spirit.

steps.label: Preaching on the way back
steps.copy: They return to Jerusalem, preaching the gospel in many Samaritan villages.

steps.label: Searching in Tarsus
steps.copy: Barnabas goes to Tarsus to look for Saul.

steps.label: A year of teaching
steps.copy: He brings him back to Antioch, and for a whole year they meet with the church and teach many people.

steps.label: Called Christians
steps.copy: In Antioch the disciples are first called Christians.

steps.label: Away to rest
steps.copy: So many are coming and going that they leave by boat for a quiet place.

steps.label: Loaves and fish
steps.copy: He blesses five loaves and two fish; all eat and are satisfied, and twelve baskets are left over.

steps.label: Walking on the sea
steps.copy: In the fourth watch of the night he comes to them walking on the water, and the wind dies down.

steps.label: Landing at Gennesaret
steps.copy: They land at Gennesaret, and people bring the sick to him wherever he goes.
